args.prompt:
Explore this codebase to understand its structure. I need to find:
1. The dashboard page/route
2. The project page/route (navigated to from dashboard)
3. How navigation between dashboard and project works
4. How data fetching / prefetching is configured (e.g. Next.js Link prefetch, loaders, route loaders, etc.)
5. What framework is being used (Next.js? Remix? React Router? etc.)

Look at package.json to determine the framework. Then find the relevant route files and components. Report back:
- The framework and version
- File paths for the dashboard route and the project route
- How the project title is fetched/loaded
- How navigation links are set up (Link components, prefetch props, etc.)
- Any loader functions or data fetching patterns used

Be thorough - check src/, app/, pages/, routes/ directories as applicable.

I have a complete and thorough understanding of the codebase. Here is my report. --- ## Framework and Version **Framework:** Next.js (App Router) **Version:** `^16.4.0-canary.24` (Next.js 16 canary) **React:** `19.1.0` Notable config detail in `/workspace/next.config.ts`: `cacheComponents: true` is enabled, which opts into Next.js's experimental/draft "Components Caching" feature. This is relevant because it changes how `use cache` and async components behave (see data fetching below). --- ## File Paths | Route | File | URL | |---|---|---| | Root layout | `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` | (all routes) | | Dashboard | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | `/` | | Project | `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` | `/projects/[slug]` (e.g. `/projects/acme`) | | Data layer | `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | (imported via `@/lib/data`) | There is no `src/`, `pages/`, or `routes/` directory — this is purely the App Router under `app/`. The only three route files are `layout.tsx`, `page.tsx` (dashboard), and `projects/[slug]/page.tsx` (project). --- ## How the Project Title Is Fetched / Loaded The project page (`/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`) uses an **async Server Component** pattern, not a `loader`/`generateMetadata`/`getServerSideProps` style fetch. There are two layers: 1. **Outer component (synchronous, default export)** — wraps the inner async component in a `` boundary with a fallback of `

Loading project...

`: ```tsx export default function ProjectPage({ params }: PageProps<'/projects/[slug]'>) { return ( Loading project...}> ) } ``` 2. **Inner async `Project` component** — awaits `params` (Next.js 16 async params), then fetches the title and details in parallel: ```tsx async function Project({ params }: Pick, 'params'>) { const { slug } = await params const [title, details] = await Promise.all([ getProjectTitle(slug), getProjectDetails(slug), ]) return

{title}

...
} ``` The data functions live in `/workspace/lib/data.ts` and both use the **`'use cache'`** directive (Next.js's caching primitive, enabled by `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts`): - **`getProjectTitle(slug)`** — marked `'use cache'`, returns `projects[slug]?.title ?? 'Unknown project'`. This is a fast lookup with no artificial delay. - **`getProjectDetails(slug)`** — marked `'use cache'`, but contains an `await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 800))` artificial 800ms delay before returning the description + activity array. The data source is an in-memory `Record` with two hardcoded projects: `acme` ("Acme Storefront") and `orbit` ("Orbit Analytics"). Key implication: Because `getProjectDetails` has an 800ms delay while `getProjectTitle` returns instantly, the `` boundary lets the title + body render as a single suspense chunk after both resolve (they're awaited together via `Promise.all`). There is **no `generateMetadata`** and **no `loading.tsx`** file — the only loading state is the inline ``. --- ## How Navigation Links Are Set Up Navigation from the dashboard to a project uses **`next/link`'s `Link`** component in `/workspace/app/page.tsx`: ```tsx import Link from 'next/link' const projects = [ { slug: 'acme', name: 'Acme Storefront' }, { slug: 'orbit', name: 'Orbit Analytics' }, ] export default function Dashboard() { return (

Projects

    {projects.map((project) => (
  • {project.name}
    • ))}
) } ``` Important observations about the `Link` usage: - **No `prefetch` prop is set** — it relies entirely on Next.js's default prefetch behavior. - **No `Link` back to the dashboard** from the project page — the project page (`/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`) has no navigation links at all; it only renders the project content. Navigation back to the dashboard is via the browser (back button / URL), not a ``. - The `href` is a dynamic template literal: `` `/projects/${project.slug}` ``. ### About prefetching behavior (Next.js 16 default) In Next.js, the default `prefetch` behavior of `` has changed across versions: - Historically (Next.js 10–14): default `prefetch={null}` prefetched the linked route's data/JS when the link entered the viewport. - Next.js 15+ changed the default so that **`` no longer prefetches by default** unless `prefetch={true}` is explicitly set (this was a notable breaking change introduced in 15.0). Given this project is on Next.js 16 canary, the default is `prefetch={false}`-equivalent — meaning **the project route is NOT prefetched on hover/in-view by default** in this codebase, since no `prefetch` prop is passed. This is a significant point: there is **no explicit prefetching configured anywhere** in this codebase — no `prefetch={true}` on any ``, no `loading.tsx`, no `generateStaticParams`, no `revalidate`, and no route-level `loader`. The only "prefetch-like" mechanism is the `'use cache'` directive on the data functions, which caches their results after the first call rather than prefetching them ahead of navigation. --- ## Loader Functions / Data Fetching Patterns Summary There are **no traditional loaders** in this codebase (no Remix-style `loader` exports, no Next.js Pages Router `getServerSideProps`/`getStaticProps`, no Next.js `generateMetadata`). The data-fetching patterns actually used are: 1. **Async Server Components** — the project page is an `async function` that `await`s data directly. This is the App Router idiom replacing loaders. 2. **`'use cache'` directive** — both data functions in `lib/data.ts` are tagged `'use cache'`, which is Next.js's caching primitive (works in tandem with `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts`). This caches the function's return value keyed by its arguments. 3. **`Promise.all` parallel fetching** — `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` are awaited concurrently. 4. **`` boundary** — wraps the async child so the page can stream; the fallback is a plain `

Loading project...

`. 5. **Async `params`** — `const { slug } = await params` reflects the Next.js 15+ async dynamic-params API. ### Other notes - The root `layout.tsx` exports a static `metadata` object (`title: 'Projects'`, `description: 'Project dashboard'`) — there is no per-project metadata generation. - The `__agent_eval__/run.mjs` file is an unrelated sandbox runner for an external agent-eval harness (OpenCode CLI invocation); it is not part of the application's routing or data fetching. The `opencode.json` is its config (contains a provider API key — you may want to treat that as a secret and avoid committing/rotating it). - `tsconfig.json` has `"@/*": ["./*"]` path alias, which is why imports use `@/lib/data`. --- ## TL;DR - **Framework:** Next.js 16 canary (`^16.4.0-canary.24`), App Router, React 19.1, with `cacheComponents: true`. - **Dashboard route:** `/workspace/app/page.tsx` (URL `/`). - **Project route:** `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` (URL `/projects/[slug]`). - **Navigation:** `next/link` `` from the dashboard, with **no `prefetch` prop** (so no explicit prefetching; Next.js 16 default is no auto-prefetch). No back-link from the project page. - **Project title fetching:** async Server Component awaits `getProjectTitle(slug)` (a `'use cache'` function in `/workspace/lib/data.ts`) via `Promise.all` alongside `getProjectDetails(slug)`, wrapped in a `` boundary. No `generateMetadata`, no `loading.tsx`, no route loaders. session_id: ses_f77943997ffeLopiXa8FWXLdho

The `PageProps` errors are pre-existing (the type is provided by Next.js's build-time types, not visible to standalone `tsc`). **What changed:** The project page previously awaited `getProjectTitle` (instant) and `getProjectDetails` (800ms delay) together via `Promise.all` inside one `Suspense` boundary, so the title was blocked behind the slow details fetch. I split them into two separate `Suspense` boundaries: - `` — awaits only `getProjectTitle`, streams in instantly. - `` — awaits `getProjectDetails`, streams in after its 800ms delay with a `

Loading details...

` fallback. No prefetching is configured anywhere (Next.js 16's default `` behavior doesn't prefetch), so the project route is only fetched on navigation — exactly as you wanted. The title now appears immediately on navigation while the rest of the page loads progressively.
